summary: H.R. 2283 directs the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to establish a three-year pilot program providing grants to eligible non-profit or outpatient mental health care providers. These grants fund culturally competent, evidence-based mental health care for veterans, including services delivered in person or via telehealth. The bill also extends certain housing loan fee expiration dates.

affected_groups.effect: Can receive culturally competent, evidence-based mental health care, including through telehealth or in person, free of charge for services funded by the grant.
May receive services like family, couples, or group therapy when integral to a veteran's successful clinical outcome.
Eligible to apply for and receive grant funding if they meet specific licensing, accreditation, and veteran-experience criteria.

key_provisions: Establishes a three-year pilot program at the VA to award grants to eligible outpatient mental health care facilities for veteran mental health care.
Sets maximum grant amounts generally at $1,500,000 per facility per fiscal year, with specific budget percentage limits for facilities receiving large shares of federal grants.
Permits grant funds to be used for care delivery, facility operation or expansion, outreach, care coordination, clinician training, and program evaluation.
Allows grant funds to be used to provide specific family and dependent mental health services, such as couples or family therapy, when clinically necessary.
Authorizes appropriations of $20,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2029 to carry out the pilot program.
Extends specific housing loan fee expiration dates from June 9, 2034, to July 24, 2034.
missing_information: Total overall nationwide budget impact beyond the authorized appropriations of $20,000,000 per year for fiscal years 2027 through 2029.
Exact number of facilities or veterans that will ultimately participate in the pilot program.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 2283 directs the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to establish a three-year pilot program providing grants to eligible non-profit or outpatient mental health care providers. These grants fund culturally competent, evidence-based mental health care for veterans, including services delivered in person or via telehealth. The bill also extends certain housing loan fee expiration dates.
summary_detail.significance: This bill initiates a focused three-year federal grant program distributing up to $20 million annually from 2027 to 2029 to expand outpatient mental health access for veterans through community-based providers, alongside minor adjustments to housing loan fee timelines.
